stem.en: Party R polled more votes across the country than Party S, yet only Party S is a national party. How can that be?

text.en: The ECI prefers Party S and is free to pick it
A party with more votes must always win fewer seats
Votes never count towards a party's recognition
Party S met one route, and Party R met none

explanation.en: Recognition uses fixed routes, and any one is enough. Party S can qualify on seats won across States, even with fewer votes. The ECI applies the same conditions to every party, and votes do count in some routes.

hints.en: Think of the line at the top of the list of conditions.
